Android only restarts a proxy from boot when this app is exempt from battery optimization. Without the exemption the tile still works, but the proxy does not come back after a reboot.
The TCP port this proxy listens on. 1080 is the SOCKS convention; two running proxies need two ports. The laptop points at this port on the phone\'s address.
The SOCKS5 user name the laptop sends. It is stored with this proxy and never shown in dumpsys or the log; the password is the only secret.
The SOCKS5 password. It lives in the app\'s private preferences, is never printed by dumpsys or the log, and is dropped entirely when the proxy listens without authentication.
The only Wi-Fi the port opens on. On this network the listener serves; on another the service stays up with the port closed and opens again when the phone comes back.
Open the port on whatever network the phone is on. Simpler, but the phone then offers the proxy on every Wi-Fi it joins — the credentials still apply.
Accept clients without a user and password. Anyone who can reach the port can then relay through the phone, so only on a network you trust.

Come back by itself: at boot, and whenever the phone joins the SSID. Android only allows that with the battery exemption and background location — phone-doctor reports and phone-proxy-boot grants both.

Switch Android\'s wireless debugging back on when the phone joins the SSID, so adb can still reach it after a reboot. That needs WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, which phone-proxy-install grants; without it the app says so instead of failing silently.
Store the form in this proxy without starting or stopping anything. Start saves first as well, so Save is for keeping a change you are not ready to run.
Throw the unsaved edits away and show what the store holds for this proxy.
Start this proxy with the settings on these pages — the form is stored first — or stop the running listener. Which one the button offers follows the state of this proxy.
Another proxy: it copies this one\'s credentials and network and takes the next free port, then opens for its own settings.
